cards.explanation: The answer is to kill them and devote them to destruction. The LORD says, “Kill them and devote them to destruction. Do all that I have commanded you…” It's a heavy one, friends. I'm not going to joke about this part. I'll just say it plainly and let it sit.

The answer is False. Babylon, the hammer of the whole earth, "…lies broken and shattered!" Think of a tool that's cracked in half on the workshop floor. Nobody's picking it up to finish the job, friends.

The answer is horror. The verse says, "What a horror Babylon has become among the nations!" That's quite a turn for a place the verse calls "…the hammer of the whole earth…" The same verse says that hammer "…lies broken and shattered!"

The answer is because she challenged the LORD. God says, "You were found and captured because you challenged the LORD." The snare isn't random, friends. The text gives the reason, and it's Babylon challenging Him.

The answer is His weapons of wrath. Here is what the verse says, friends: "The LORD has opened His armory and brought out His weapons of wrath…" The verse also says this is the work of the Lord GOD of Hosts in the land of the Chaldeans. The armory is His, the weapons are His, and the work is His.
The answer is False. The order is to "Devote her to destruction; leave her no survivors." There's no room for a few survivors in that line. It's a heavy one, friends, so I'll just say it straight.

The answer is the vengeance of the LORD for His temple. The fugitives and refugees are "…declaring in Zion the vengeance of the LORD our God, the vengeance for His temple." They've gotten out of Babylon, and what they carry into Zion is a declaration about the LORD, friends. It isn't about themselves.

The answer is deeds. The order is, "Repay her according to her deeds; do to her as she has done." The verse says she has defied the LORD, the Holy One of Israel. The repayment is measured by what she did, friends.

The answer is no one at all. The verse says, "The arrogant one will stumble and fall with no one to pick him up." He falls, and no one picks him up. It's a hard picture, friends, and I think that's the point of it.

The answer is True. God says, “And I will kindle a fire in his cities to consume all those around him.” It's right there in the verse, friends. He speaks of cities, and the fire reaches those around him.

The answer is their Redeemer. "Their Redeemer is strong; the LORD of Hosts is His name." The verse before it says their captors hold them fast and refuse to release them. Right after that, the text puts the strength on the Redeemer's side. Israel and Judah aren't left with only their own muscle, friends.

The answer is turmoil. He will plead their case "…so that He may bring rest to the earth, but turmoil to those who live in Babylon." Rest goes to the earth, and turmoil goes to Babylon's residents. The verse sets those two side by side, friends.
The answer is False. The verse says, "A sword is against her false prophets, and they will become fools." The word is fools, not wise, friends. That's why this one is False.

The answer is terror. "A sword is against her warriors, and they will be filled with terror." These are the fighters, friends, the ones who are supposed to be steady. The verse says terror fills them. The same verse has a sword against her false prophets too.

The answer is plundered. "A sword is against her treasuries, and they will be plundered." What was stored up gets taken, friends. The same verse also has a sword against her horses and chariots. It's the opposite of a savings plan working out.

The answer is that it is a land of graven images. That's the reason the verse gives, friends: "A drought is upon her waters, and they will be dried up. For it is a land of graven images, and the people go mad over idols." The text ties the drought to the images and the idols. It doesn't give any other reason here.

The answer is Sodom and Gomorrah. The LORD says, "As God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah along with their neighbors, no one will dwell there; no man will abide there." The comparison is about the place staying empty, friends. Those two cities are the picture the LORD chose.

The answer is great. The verse says, "a great nation and many kings are stirred up from the ends of the earth." Notice it's a great nation plus many kings, friends. The verse also says an army is coming from the north. That's a lot of folks heading Babylon's way.

The answer is that they hang limp. "The king of Babylon has heard the report, and his hands hang limp." The verse adds, "Anguish has gripped him, pain like that of a woman in labor." One report and his hands give out, friends.

The answer is the thickets of the Jordan. "Behold, one will come up like a lion from the thickets of the Jordan to the watered pasture." That's the spot the verse names, friends. Then God says, "…in an instant I will chase Babylon from her land." I always picture a lion coming out of tall brush when nobody expected it.
The answer is False. God says, "For in an instant I will chase Babylon from her land." That's quick, friends. Even a batch of cookies takes longer than an instant.

The answer is quake. The verse says, "At the sound of Babylon’s capture the earth will quake…" The quake belongs to the moment of that sound, friends. The verse goes on to say a cry will be heard among the nations.

The answer is True. The verse says, "At the sound of Babylon’s capture the earth will quake; a cry will be heard among the nations." The cry goes out among the nations, friends. It's the second half of that line, right after the quake.
